key_insight: LLM agents often solve decomposition benchmarks correctly, but checking the final answer alone can miss failures to implement the prescribed algorithm.
engineering_relevance: Reliable AI-generated optimization solvers need execution tests, feasibility and objective checks, and code-level method audits with targeted repair feedback.
method: Introduce DecompGym: 81 instances across five Benders decomposition and four column-generation problem families.
Require execution within 60 seconds, numerical feasibility, an LLM-based method audit, and an objective within 1% of the stored optimum.
Evaluate 12 models over up to ten attempts, comparing independent regeneration with failure-diagnosing reflection.
evidence_signal: Two models solved all instances on the first attempt; reflection converted 66% of retries into successes versus 39% for regeneration, while output-only checks would accept 93 of 108 attempts rejected by the method audit.
watch_item: Method compliance is assessed by an LLM judge, so audit reliability remains an implementation concern.
paper_title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
